findings.observation: Read the Engineer's Summary Letter (documentId: ca527d05-4b8e-4723-9fb5-d6ad29965e35). Section 02 'Utilities and Stormwater Management' states: 'Underground water quality and detention ponds are proposed on-site to collect, treat, and detain the stormwater runoff on site for the 2-, 10-, 25-, and 100-year storm events per the City of Austin ECM and DCM requirements.' Section 03 'Access, Erosion Control, and Signatures' shows the letter is signed by Shelly Mitchell, P.E., with PE seal #103662 and dated 04/23/2026. The letter explicitly mentions both 2-year peak flow control (by listing 2-year storm events) and WQ compliance (by stating water quality ponds will 'treat' stormwater).
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires the engineer's project summary letter to be present, signed/sealed/dated, and explicitly discuss 2-yr peak flow control and WQ compliance. The Engineer's Summary Letter meets all criteria: it is signed by Shelly Mitchell PE, sealed with #103662, dated 04/23/2026, and explicitly addresses both 2-year peak flow control (detention for 2-year storm) and water quality compliance (treatment via WQ ponds). Both topics are directly addressed in the stormwater management paragraph.
findings.explanation: Engineer's summary letter signed/sealed/dated 04/23/2026 and explicitly discusses 2-year peak flow control and water quality compliance.

findings.observation: Reviewed the Engineering and Drainage Report Section 03 'Drainage and Detention' and Section 04 'Water Quality and Environmental'. The drainage section documents detention pond analysis for 2-, 10-, 25-, and 100-year storm events, showing proposed peak flows are less than existing flows at all three analysis points. The report states the site 'has been determined to be outside the 100-year floodplain and the City of Austin fully developed floodplain' and confirms 'According to the Travis County, Texas FEMA Flood map number 48453C0445K, effective January 22, 2020, the subject property does not lie within a FEMA floodplain.' Called semantic search for 'RSMP Regional Stormwater Management Program application' which returned no RSMP-related content. Confirmed in facts.md that 'RSMP Participation: No'.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires either flood control compliance documentation OR an RSMP application. While no RSMP application is included, flood control compliance IS documented. The Engineering and Drainage Report demonstrates compliance with LDC § 25-7-61(A)(5)(c) 2-year peak flow control requirement through on-site detention analysis, and documents that the site is outside the floodplain. The absence of an RSMP application does not constitute a failure when flood control compliance is documented through traditional on-site detention methods.
findings.explanation: Flood control compliance documented via detention pond analysis for 2-, 10-, 25-, and 100-year storms in drainage report.
